About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.

If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month-not next year-this is your playground.

 

Position Summary

You are the second half of a two-person machine shop, working alongside our Machine Shop Manager to keep the spindles turning across a wider band of hours than one person can. You bring about five years of stick time on CNC mills and lathes, you program your own parts in Mastercam, and you handle the rest of a working shop: manual machines, sawing, deburring, tapping, fitting and inspection. The shop builds the hardware EDDA's R&D and test program runs on - turret structure, mounts, drive parts, fixtures and test rigs - often from a CAD model that landed that morning.

 
 

Essential Duties

- Program your own parts: CAD to toolpaths in Mastercam, tooling, speeds and feeds, prove-out at the machine, G-code edits at the control.

- Set up and run CNC mills and lathes: workholding, offsets, probing, first article to print, then hold tolerance across the run.

- Do the rest of the shop's work: manual mill and lathe, saw, drill press, tapping, deburring, press fits and inserts, light fitting and assembly.

- Inspect and document: hand tools on a surface plate, GD&T, first-article records - in aluminum, steel, stainless, plastics and the occasional titanium.

- Run the shop with the manager: split and stagger the queue, hand off cleanly, give engineers honest lead times and DFM feedback, keep the machines maintained and the shop safe and clean.

 

Requirements

- Experience: about 5 years (3-7) in a working machine shop, with real stick time on both CNC mills and CNC lathes.

- CNC programming (required): you write your own programs from CAD in CAM - we run Mastercam - read and edit G-code at the control, and have proven out your own programs. Running someone else's program does not meet this bar.

- Setup and operation: workholding, fixturing, tool and work offsets, first-article proof-out; you hold ±0.001" when the print calls for it.

- General shop process and inspection: manual machining, sawing, drilling, tapping, deburring and fitting; read GD&T and inspect with calipers, micrometers, height and bore gauges.

- Flexible schedule: willing to work a staggered shift coordinated with the Machine Shop Manager - early starts some weeks, late finishes others.

- Compliance and physical: U.S. citizenship, ability to pass a background check, lift 50 lb and stand for long periods.

 

Nice‑to‑Have

- Prototype or R&D shop background: one-offs, fast turnaround, incomplete drawings, engineers at your elbow.

- 4th/5-axis milling, live-tooling lathes, Fanuc macros and probing cycles.

- CAD, not just CAM: model a fixture or simple part in SolidWorks and design your own workholding.

- Secondary processes: TIG welding, sheet metal, 3-D printing, or spec'ing anodize, plating and heat treat.

- Weapon, firearms, aerospace or defense hardware; security clearance or the ability to obtain one.

 

Benefits

Le poste est à pourvoir au sein du Centre RAPSODEE (Recherche d'Albi en génie des Procédés des SOlides Divisés, de l'Energie et de l'Environnement), unité mixte de recherche CNRS dédiée aux procédés, matériaux et énergies durables.
Le Postdoc sera dirigé par le professeur Ange Nzihou et codirigé par un chercheur de l'université de Princeton (États-Unis).

DESCRIPTION DU POSTE :
Ce travail s’inscrit dans un projet ERC (European Research Council) Advanced Grant. L’ERC est une organisation européenne de financement qui soutient des projets de recherche de rupture à travers des appels à projets très compétitifs, dans le cadre du programme Horizon Europe de l’Union européenne.
Le projet ERC vise à évaluer la capacité de stockage de composites innovants en biocarbones. Il s’agit d’une famille de matériaux carbonés avancés et durables issus de la biomasse, permettant de stocker l’énergie dans différents environnements, contrairement à la plupart des solutions actuelles reposant sur des matériaux d’origine fossile ou non durables. Cela devrait se traduire par une réduction notable des émissions de CO₂ et des économies d’énergie. L’objectif est de développer et d’appliquer des modèles numériques, des méthodes fondées sur les données et des outils utilisant l’IA afin de prédire les propriétés des matériaux, d’optimiser leur composition et leur structure, et d’améliorer la capacité et les performances de stockage de l’énergie. Les travaux combineront des études théoriques et numériques avec la synthèse expérimentale, la caractérisation, la validation et l’optimisation de solutions innovantes de stockage de l’énergie.
Un axe important du projet portera sur l’étude des propriétés thermophysiques, thermomécaniques et de stabilité thermique de composites à base de biocarbone graphitique. Le/La candidat(e) étudiera les relations entre la structure des matériaux, leurs propriétés fonctionnelles, leur comportement et les performances globales du dispositif en conditions d’utilisation, afin de contribuer au développement de technologies de stockage de l’énergie sûres, efficaces et durables.

INFORMATION SYSTEMS SECURITY ENGINEER (PRINCIPAL)

ABOUT THE ROLE

Snowflake's national security deployments are authorized to operate inside classified environments, and each authorization stands or falls on the security documentation behind it. This role owns that documentation. You assess the system against its security control baseline, assemble the evidence the authorizing official reviews, and you are accountable for the package getting to authorization on schedule.

Arc Reactor, a classified deployment for a US government customer, is the immediate assignment. The same work will apply to the deployments that follow it.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Lead the security control assessment for an assigned deployment, from control selection and tailoring through the body of evidence to authorization.

- Produce the assessment plan, the evidence collection schedule and the residual risk that goes to the authorizing official, and keep them current.

- Direct the engineers and security staff producing control artifacts. Tell them which evidence to collect, review what they produce, and catch gaps in the requirements before they surface during assessment.

- Be the person who can explain a Snowflake control implementation to a government security reviewer, and explain a reviewer's finding back to the engineering team in terms they can act on.

- Track authorization status and blockers, and report them weekly to the engineering lead and the program.

WHAT YOU BRING

- You have taken at least one system through authorization to operate under a government security control framework (NIST 800-53 / RMF, FedRAMP, or the DoD RMF and its Impact Levels), and you can point to the package you were responsible for.

- You can read an engineering implementation and decide which control it satisfies and what evidence it produces.

- You have worked with government authorizing officials or security control assessors, and you know what they reject and why.

- You write the plan down. Assessment scope, control status, evidence gaps and residual risk live in a document the team can run without you, not in your head.

- You are eligible for TS/SCI with a full-scope polygraph, or already hold it.

HOW THIS TEAM WORKS

The ISSE does not work alone and does not do all the collection. Engineers and supporting security staff produce the artifacts; you decide what is needed, review it, and own the result. The role reports into national security engineering and sits in the deployment's weekly engineering and security cadence. The work is done from the Washington, DC area, with regular time on site.

About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC, 

About the team

Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Cloudflare's network runs in hundreds of cities on general-purpose Linux servers, not dedicated routers, so the routers, firewalls, load balancers, and proxies that carry our customers' traffic are software that we write, ship, and operate ourselves.

Our Packet Processing team builds and operates that software: high-performance code that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare's network, in every Cloudflare data center. That includes the L4 load balancer at the front door of every server, a per-customer routing and forwarding data plane, a stateful network firewall, and a TCP/UDP reverse proxy (the engines behind products like Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, and Spectrum).

We are a team of engineers who obsess over performance, correctness, and reliability at massive scale. We own what we build in production, a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC.

About the role

For us, performance is a product feature. Customers notice single-flow throughput, packet loss, and latency right away, and every CPU cycle we spend on a packet is multiplied across every server in our network. We're looking for engineers who love finding out where the time goes, and then making it go away.

Some of the things you'd work on:

• Pushing single large flows (e.g., one tunnel carrying a customer's whole data center) to multiple Gbps and beyond, and making that performance consistent

• Finding out exactly where packets get dropped and why: NIC queues, interrupts and softirq, XDP, veth and namespaces, userspace rings, and everything in between

• CPU placement: NUMA, RSS, core isolation, and steering traffic to the right cores on servers that also run many other services
